messages:
Maya: Quick question — who's authorized to flip the emergency feature toggle for rollout_payments_v2 in prod? Need to update the runbook.
Alex: Short answer: eng-oncall (current oncall) + SRE lead + Platform oncall. Product can request a flip but cannot execute without oncall.
Sanjay: Agreed. Add a rule: anything that affects >10% traffic or P95 latency gets immediate oncall authority. Otherwise, PO + eng owner approval is required.
Liz: Also mandatory process when flipping: 1) create an incident ticket, 2) run the toggle command, 3) post link to ticket in #incidents and the product channel, 4) set a rollback ETA. ops-bot will emit an audit event automatically.
Maya: Can you paste the exact CLI and how to verify the audit? Saving to the runbook.
Liz: CLI we use (prod only):
```
flagctl toggle --env=prod --flag=rollout_payments_v2 --action=disable --reason="latency spike"
```
Audit quick-check (flag-audit service):
```
SELECT * FROM flag_audit WHERE flag='rollout_payments_v2' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 10;
```
That returns who ran it, their id, and the reason.
Sanjay: Important: only users in role `flag_admin` can execute flagctl against prod. To audit role membership: `idp-cli members --role flag_admin`. Runbook should include that exact command.
Alex: Ops-bot will also log flips to /var/log/flags and send a webhook to the incident-creator automation. We have an automated rule that opens a ticket when a prod toggle is flipped.
Ops-bot: [automated] If a toggle is flipped in prod, an incident will be created and #eng-oncall will be pinged within 90s.
Paul: Small ops note: if disabling a feature that backs downstream queues, pause the queues first or you'll create huge backpressure. Added to the checklist.
Maya: Helpful — I'll update infra-runbooks/feature-toggle.md and open a PR. tagging @Liz for the snippet and @Alex for oncall wording.
Liz: ack :thumbsup:
Alex: Also include a short escalation ladder: oncall -> SRE lead -> Eng manager -> CTO for socio-technical escalations. And require Slack permalink of authorization in the incident.
Maya: Will do. I'll link the PR here once ready.
Sanjay: One more: include a section that defines "full kill" vs "canary pause" and the exact traffic percentages for each. Keeps the ambiguity out of handoffs.
Maya: Good call. Thanks everyone.
Paul: 👍
